governing_intent: Prove an offline, event-driven continuous-factory walking skeleton with deterministic doubles, durable restart recovery, priority/dependency/WIP scheduling, and rolling refill, without vendor access, provider spend, Node changes, or a Python-Sovereignty claim.
summary: The BIU is tightly bounded, its requirement extents are candid, and most acceptance criteria are observable through executable deterministic integration tests. It has one material authority conflict: it requires lifecycle progress through VERIFY, REVIEW, ACCEPT, and DONE while excluding candidate-custody mechanics, real workers, network access, and PY-06; the approved candidate-custody invariant requires a durably retrievable exact candidate for a fresh independent verifier before VERIFY.
owner_clarifications: Must PY-04 receive an explicit, bounded test-only exception to the candidate-publication and independent-verifier requirements for its offline scripted-worker path, or must its scope be changed so it does not cross VERIFY/ACCEPT/DONE until PY-06 supplies real candidate custody and verifier invocation? The current authorities do not authorize treating an unverified scripted outcome as a substitute for that invariant.
implementation_unknowns: Concrete WorkManagement and WorkerProvider port signatures, outcome/event payloads, and typed rejection shapes.
The deterministic fixture format, event-delivery harness, process entrypoint used only by the restart test, and run-summary schema.
The exact SQLite recovery transaction sequencing using the PY-03 OperationalStore.
The mechanical assertions for release provenance, ordering traces, no-repeat reconcile reads, and stop reasons.
verification_assessment: The specified proof is real and mechanically testable for loop behavior: deterministic doubles exercise the coordinator rather than mocked coordinator internals; restart must be a real process restart; and ordering, WIP, refill, blocked-dependency, no-polling, release-policy, and stop-reason assertions are observable. It is not presently valid proof of the claimed full lifecycle because the contract supplies neither an authorized test-only custody/verifier exception nor PY-06 candidate custody and independent verification.
material_risks: An implementer may bypass PY-02's VERIFY-entry custody guard to make the scripted loop reach DONE.
An implementer may accidentally build a partial PY-06 custody/verifier system inside PY-04, broadening scope and duplicating later work.
A scripted success could be recorded as verification or acceptance despite the definition/observation/verdict boundary.
The OFF release-policy test could accidentally inject execution directly rather than exercising the same attributable release boundary as automatic ON.
next_action: Obtain the single custody/VERIFY boundary decision, then amend PY-04's lifecycle scope and acceptance criteria to state the approved offline test path precisely before implementation readiness is granted.
rationale: Approved authority resolves priority ownership, release ON/OFF policy, event-driven refill, WIP defaults, durable recovery, port layering, and the test-only status of the scripted worker; their lower-level realization is delegated engineering work. But SF-REQ-007 and PY-02 explicitly prohibit entering VERIFY without a durably retrievable candidate, and the architecture requires independent verifier inputs. PY-04 currently mandates VERIFY-to-DONE while expressly excluding the capabilities that establish those conditions, creating an owner-level authorization gap rather than a normal implementation unknown.
